children: Albemarle swung to a profit and reported higher revenue in the third quarter, boosted by strong demand for lithium and higher energy-storage pricing.

The specialty chemicals producer on Wednesday posted a profit of $296.8 million, or $2.15 a share, in the quarter ended Sept. 30. That compares with a loss of $160.7 million, or $1.72 a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted earnings were $2.58 a share. Analysts polled by FactSet were expecting $2.53 a share.
Revenue rose 19%, to $1.55 billion. Analysts were expecting $1.52 billion in revenue.
The company attributed its growth to a 68% increase in pricing in its energy-storage business, as well as higher volumes and prices in its specialties business.

"Global lithium demand is up 48% year-to-date [through] August, driven by both electric vehicles and energy storage, reinforcing our confidence in the long-term outlook for the industry," Chief Executive Officer Kent Masters said.

Albemarle also lowered its outlook for full-year capital expenditures to a range of $300 million to $350 million, down from its previous view of around $500 million. The updated guidance in part reflects benefits from the company's capital-efficiency improvements, it said.
